### 3.1 close_10_ema — Short-Term Trend (Bullish, Flattening)
The 10 EMA turned up on 8/11 ($143.50) and has risen in an orderly staircase to **$159.14** (8/28). Price ($161.61) sits **above the EMA**, confirming a healthy short-term uptrend. However, the slope has visibly flattened in the last week ($158.07 → $158.72 → $159.14), signaling **decelerating momentum** — the easy recovery move is maturing.

### 3.2 MACD — Regime Change Confirmed, but Plateauing
- **7/29:** −4.40 (deeply bearish at the price low)
- **8/14:** +0.35 (**zero-line crossover** — bullish regime change)
- **8/21:** peak **+2.39**
- **8/28:** +2.14 (still positive, easing)

The zero-line cross in mid-August was the highest-conviction signal of this recovery. The subsequent pullback from 2.39 to ~2.1 without a price breakdown is normal consolidation, but a drop below ~+1.9 would warn of fading momentum.

### 3.3 MACD Signal — Crossover Trigger Long Since Fired
The signal line crossed above zero on 8/18 and the MACD line has held above it since ~8/13 — a **24-day uninterrupted bullish posture**. Histogram compression (peak ~1.74 on 8/21 → ~0.53 on 8/28) confirms momentum is decelerating, **not reversing** — bullish-but-cooling.

### 3.4 RSI — Neutral, Healthy Reset (Neither Extended nor Washed Out)
- **7/29 (price low):** 33.6 — capitulation extreme
- **8/10:** 40.9 — bottoming
- **8/17:** 58.7 — recovery peak
- **8/28:** **52.6** — dead neutral

RSI has spent the last two weeks oscillating 44–59. **No overbought condition exists** (nowhere near 70), meaning the rally has not yet reached exhaustion. Equally, there's no oversold edge for dip-buyers. In this name, sub-40 RSI readings (7/29) have marked reliable bottoms; a pullback into the low-40s with price holding $155+ would be a higher-quality entry than chasing here.

### 3.5 Bollinger Upper Band — Overhead Boundary at ~$175
Upper band: **$174.99** (8/28). Note the contraction from $193.86 (7/29) — the envelope is tightening. The 8/17 rejection at $178.43 (band was $178.66 that day) shows the upper band is functioning as **real resistance**. A decisive close above ~$175 on expanding volume would signal a breakout toward the $180–195 supply zone.

### 3.6 Bollinger Lower Band — Rising Floor at ~$135
Lower band: **$134.82** and **rising** (from $119.39 on 8/10). The July collapse drove price through the lower band (capitulation); the August recovery has been a disciplined mid-band reversion. The rising lower band is structural support — the entire envelope is tilting upward, which is characteristic of a **bottoming-then-basing process**.

ATR collapsed from **$18.71 (7/31) → $10.36 (8/28)** — volatility has nearly halved during the recovery, which is exactly what orderly accumulation looks like. **Caveat:** ATR is still ~**6.4% of price per day**, roughly 3–5× a typical large-cap. Any position must be sized for this: a 2×ATR stop below a $161 entry = ~$141 — far too loose; use structure-based stops instead (below $155) with reduced size.

### 3.8 VWMA — Volume Confirms the Recovery (Accumulation Footprint)
VWMA has risen relentlessly since 8/17 (**$146.90 → $159.92**) and price is holding just above it ($161.61 vs $159.92). Critically, the largest up-move day of August (8/13: +7.3%, 32.5M shares vs ~20M average) came on the heaviest volume — **up-days are being traded with more weight than down-days**, the signature of institutional accumulation. A close below the VWMA with conviction volume would be the first warning of distribution.
